dedupe_keys.name: drivendata and noaa magnet solar wind ace dscovr and dst index data for real time geomagnetic storm forecasting

description: MagNet: Model the Geomagnetic Field is a DrivenData challenge run with NOAA to forecast the Disturbance Storm-Time index (Dst), the measure of geomagnetic storm severity. Contents: real-time solar wind measurements from NASA's Advanced Composition Explorer (ACE) and NOAA's Deep Space Climate Observatory (DSCOVR) at the L1 point as inputs, and hourly Dst values, averaged from four near-equatorial ground magnetic observatories, as labels; models had to predict Dst for the current and next hour from data up to the time of prediction, robust to sensor malfunctions and noise, scored by root mean squared error. Producer: DrivenData with the NOAA/CIRES geomagnetism group; Dst drives NOAA/NCEI's High Definition Geomagnetic Model - Real Time. Coverage: global index, multi-year solar wind record. Format and access: competition data after sign-up, an open data section on the challenge page, and code-submission winners released under the MIT licence per the rules. Licence: governed by the competition terms. Caveats: Dst is a single global index and does not give local geoelectric fields; extreme storms are rare in the record. Simulation uses: space weather hazard inputs for geomagnetically induced current studies on power grids, and warning lead times for GNSS and satellite communication operators. Related records: case_study-hydro-quebec-march-1989-geomagnetic-blackout, model-kasi-geomagnetic-storm-forecast-model and case_study-lloyds-cambridge-extreme-space-weather-scenario.
